title: Inverse image, tensor product and extension by zero preserve $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite and all schemes Noetherian.

1. For $f\colon X\to Y$ and $K\in\Dbc(Y,\cO_E)$, $f^*K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$.
2. For $K,M\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{E,X}}M\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ (no completion is
   needed).
3. For a locally closed immersion $a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S\hookrightarrow X$
   and $L\in\Dbc(S,\cO_E)$, $a_!L=i_*u_!L\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$.
4. For $a$ as in (3), $L\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ and $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$,
   $(a_!L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\simeq a_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^*M)$.

proof.text: Exact inverse image preserves bounds. Its homology comparison and pullback_constantModelConstructible preserve each constructible cohomology sheaf.
Apply the integral tensor closure theorem, proved by the degree-zero sheaf calculation and two bounded truncation inductions.

Apply constant-model immersion preservation to each cohomology sheaf, using exactness and the homology comparison. Apply first open extension by zero, then closed direct image. The latter is canonically its total right derived functor.

Apply the closed projection isomorphism to j!L and M. Inside its closed direct image apply the open projection isomorphism to L and i*M. Compose with the derived inverse-image composition isomorphism j*i*M ~= (j followed by i)*M. This proves the locally closed formula for arbitrary unbounded L,M.

tool_uses.why: Base change of a finite stratification supplies the strata for pullback and common refinement; the integral-model unit has no separate stratification lemma.
Exactness, adjunctions and complementary vanishings of module immersion functors give extension preservation and the closed projection formula; these are general pro-etale topos identities.
The general unbounded monoidal pullback theorem transports each local tensor and preserves the K-flat resolutions needed in the open projection formula.
The scalar valuation ring is a DVR with a uniformizer and unit-times-power decomposition; these scalar facts are not an operation-preservation clause.
Conservativity of finite stratum restrictions detects the tensor cohomology bounds and the closed projection-map isomorphism.
Exactness of derived tensor supports the two finite truncation inductions, and the explicitly defined mate supplies the canonical closed projection map.
The small pro-etale site over an open is the slice site, allowing the general ringed-slice tensor identity to apply.
Unbounded module complexes on a ringed site admit K-flat resolutions with flat terms, used to prove the open projection formula without boundedness assumptions.
The sheaf-level tensor identity for extension from a slice yields the open derived formula bidegree by bidegree; it does not restate the integral constructibility clauses.
Composition of inverse-image functors identifies a^* with u^* i^* when the two immersion formulas are composed.
Exact sheafification carries the injective scalar constant-presheaf map to an injective constant-sheaf map before flat change of coefficients; this is a general site tool.
